segments: Generation management in NixOS mainly uses three command families: nixos-rebuild, nix-env, and nix-collect-garbage. The core operations are listing, switching, deleting, and cleaning up. Combined with automatic maintenance options in configuration.nix, they can run unattended. The following are maintenance examples; confirm the target profile and required rollback window before running them.
1. Overview of the generation lifecycle

switch/boot can record a new generation when updating the system profile. Running only build or test does not establish a new system profile generation. Old generations are generally retained until manual or automatic maintenance deletes them. The ability to roll back depends on which profiles and outputs remain. The corresponding /nix/store paths are actually freed only after generations are explicitly deleted and garbage collection runs.

Tip: nix-collect-garbage -d is equivalent to first running nix-env --delete-generations old on the profiles the tool finds, then running nix-store --gc. Afterward, you cannot roll back to deleted generations.
3. Freeing space in /nix/store
1. Standard two-step cleanup
This procedure limits history deletion to the specified system profile. Delete generations before running GC; otherwise, packages referenced by those generations will not be collected.
2. Optimize storage (deduplicate with hard links)
Deduplicate identical store file contents using hard links. Space savings depend on how much content is duplicated; this can be run regularly alongside GC.
4. Configure automatic maintenance in configuration.nix
Add these options to /etc/nixos/configuration.nix and rebuild to enable automatic cleanup without running commands manually:

nix.gc.automatic is the officially recommended approach to prevent /nix/store from growing without bound. boot.loader.grub.configurationLimit limits the number of GRUB menu entries at the source, keeping the boot list from becoming too long.
5. Advanced tips
1. Simplify operations with nh
nh (nix helper) is a popular community wrapper. It provides friendlier commands such as nh os switch and nh os generations, and can display a configuration diff after rebuilding.
2. The newer nix commands

This pattern is common in community configuration repositories.
3. Roll back when the system cannot boot

Even if the system cannot reach the desktop, NixOS retains a "NixOS - All configurations" submenu in GRUB by default. It lists historical generations that have not been deleted and fall within the boot-menu retention limit. Select one to return to a previous working state; this is the last safety net.
4. Safe cleanup recommendations
Before running nix-collect-garbage -d, confirm that the current generation is stable, because deleted generations cannot be used for rollback.
On production servers, prefer --delete-older-than 30d over -d to retain a rollback window.

After a major version upgrade, verify operation and the rollback procedure before cleaning up according to your retention policy. Limiting menu entries does not automatically delete profile history or free all store space.

Together, these commands and settings cover most needs from everyday rollback to long-term disk maintenance: inspect status with nixos-rebuild list-generations, use --rollback in emergencies, clean up regularly with nix-collect-garbage --delete-older-than, and add nix.gc.automatic as an automatic fallback.
